facts.value: Developers must submit an energy plan to the Energy and Environment Cabinet showing protection of residential ratepayers and assuring that energy needs can be met now, in the near term and long term without additional costs to other utility ratepayers.
facts.supporting_quote: Data center project developers are required to submit an energy plan to the Energy and Environment Cabinet showing how it will protect residential ratepayers, including assurances it can meet its energy needs now, into the near term, and long term without imposing additional costs on other utility ratepayers.

facts.value: The Public Service Commission shall not allow a utility to recover data-center development and operation costs by increasing rates paid by other ratepayers.
facts.supporting_quote: The Public Service Commission shall not allow a utility to increase rates paid by other ratepayers to recover costs caused by the development and operation of a data center.

facts.value: The Energy and Environment Cabinet is directed to deny permitting applications where a data center would negatively affect the listed environmental resources.
facts.supporting_quote: The Energy and Environment Cabinet is directed to deny any permitting applications where a data center would negatively impact Kentucky’s air quality, water use, water quality, water supply, federal jurisdictional wetlands, or natural resources.

facts.value: Developers must demonstrate compliance with applicable environmental laws and public-engagement requirements.
facts.supporting_quote: Data center developers must also demonstrate compliance with all applicable environmental laws and public engagement requirements.

facts.value: Developers must commit to paying their full and fair share of state and local taxes and not attempt to avoid taxes, especially those for local communities and schools.

facts.value: Developers must commit to public discussions with local leaders and members and transparently address community questions, including local job opportunities.

field_decisions.value: Requires data-center developers to submit energy plans protecting residential ratepayers and assuring energy needs can be met now, in the near term and long term without additional costs to other utility ratepayers. Directs the Public Service Commission not to allow utilities to increase rates paid by other ratepayers to recover costs caused by data-center development and operation. Directs the Energy and Environment Cabinet to deny permit applications where a data center would negatively affect listed environmental resources and requires compliance with applicable environmental laws and public-engagement requirements. Requires tax and community-engagement commitments and preserves local-community decisions on data-center operations. The order does not establish a categorical moratorium or repeal all statutory incentives.
